text:
OpsAlertBot: :rotating_light: AUTO-DETECT us-east-4: host I/O error rate >99p. ~70% GPU hosts reporting block device timeouts, control-plane API 502/503 spike. Auto-drain attempts failing. Opening triage channel.

Maya: On it. pulling journalctl -u node-agent --since "15m" and /var/log/kern.log. dmesg showing repeated nvme reset loops. attaching sanitized snippets.

Arjun: Storage team pinged. Two SAN controllers reported a failover but host NVMe paths aren't switching cleanly. VendorEng, can you join?

Priya: Scheduler note: many pods stuck Terminating; kubelet can't detach volumes so drains are hanging. Will cordon then evict gracefully where possible; keep stateful workload caution.

Len: Traffic ops here. Kicking off gradual traffic shift off us-east-4: routectl shift --from us-east-4 --to us-east-2,us-east-1 --weights 50,20. Aim to reduce load and give room for evacuation.

Zoe: I'll post a short incident banner and spin up a status page entry. Draft: "Partial regional outage in us-east-4 affecting inference latency. Traffic being shifted; mitigation in progress. Next update in 20m."

StorageBot: Vendor ticket 900112 opened. SAN vendor sees high pending queue depth on controller A and recommends activating secondary fabric path or firmware rollback. ETA for failover path engage ~30-60m.

Maya: dmesg snippet (sanitized):
``n[ 2345.123456] nvme0n1: I/O error, aborting commands
[ 2345.223456] Buffer I/O error on device nvme0n1, logical block 987654
[ 2345.500001] nvme-core: resetting controller
```

Arjun: Proposed mitigation checklist: 1) enable host multipath failover, 2) run safe-detach to force-clean stale mounts where possible, 3) suspend noncritical batch/model training and deprioritize background cache writes. infra-sre to run scripts.

Priya: Cordon+drain executed on 16 nodes so far. Forced kubelet restarts helped some drains; 6 nodes still unreachable with I/O errors. Evicted ~120 pods, gave priority to critical inference services.

Len: Requesting emergency capacity: launching 40 GPUs in us-east-2 (reserved warm pool) and 10 in us-west-1 as standby. Raised quota bump with cloud ops for expedited allocation.

Zoe: Customer comms posted to status.redwood.com and support channel. Marking incident P1 and opening banner for major tenants.

VendorEng: Confirming SAN controller firmware regression on 2026-03 build observed in limited cases. Activating secondary fabric path should restore most hosts; we expect progressive recovery in 30-60m if path clean.

Maya: After traffic shift we see control-plane latency drop ~35%. Some tenants still see tail latency if pinned to us-east-4; enabling per-tenant throttles and fallback model variants with smaller KV caches to reduce disk pressure.

Arjun: Longer-term followups: schedule rolling reboots with safe evacuation, apply NVMe driver update (or firmware rollback) across affected pools, and add improved multipath tests to CI. For now keep traffic shifted and monitor vendor remediation.

OpsAlertBot: Incident INC-2026-913 created. priority=P1. First triage complete. Next update in 20m or on any major state change. Participants: Maya, Arjun, Priya, Len, Zoe, StorageBot, OpsAlertBot, VendorEng.
